extracted.intended_audience: members of the public seeking records or corrections and Commission staff (System Manager, Freedom of Information Officer, Chairman) responsible for FOIA/Privacy Act/section 504 compliance
extracted.subtask_description: Procedures and standards for requesting access to, amendment of, and disclosure of Commission records under the Privacy Act and the Freedom of Information Act, plus related definitions, fees, appeals, and section 504 self‑evaluation requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Purpose and scope (Privacy Act procedures)
rubrics_metrics.description: These procedures provide the means by which individuals may safeguard their privacy by obtaining access to, and requesting amendments or corrections in, information about these individuals which is under the control of the National Capital Planning Commission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Establishes that the rules govern access and amendment requests to Commission-controlled personal information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of individual (Privacy Act)
rubrics_metrics.description: The term individual means a citizen of the United States or an alien lawfully admitted for permanent residence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Determines who may make Privacy Act requests under these procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of maintain
rubrics_metrics.description: The term maintain includes maintain, collect, use, or disseminate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used to define the Commission's actions covered by the Privacy Act rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of record (Privacy Act)
rubrics_metrics.description: The term record means any item, collection or grouping of information about an individual that is maintained by the Commission ... and that contains his or her name, or the identifying number, symbol, or other identifying particular assigned to the individual, such as social security number.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies what information constitutes a 'record' for access/amendment purposes (payroll info, mailing address, identifiers, etc.).

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of system of records (Privacy Act)
rubrics_metrics.description: The term system of records means a group of any records under the control of the Commission from which information is retrieved by the name of the individual or by some identifying number, symbol, or other identifying particular assigned to the individual.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Determines the scope of record systems subject to Privacy Act procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of routine use (Privacy Act)
rubrics_metrics.description: The term routine use means, with respect to the disclosure of a record, the use of such record for a purpose which is compatible with the purpose for which it was collected.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Limits permissible disclosures consistent with original collection purposes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedure to determine whether a system contains a record (§455.3(a))
rubrics_metrics.description: An individual shall submit a written request to the appropriate System Manager; the System Manager shall, within 10 days of receipt, inform the individual whether a system of records maintained by the Commission contains such a record.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Written inquiries to System Manager; 10‑day response requirement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Access request content and delivery option (§455.3(b))
rubrics_metrics.description: An individual desiring access to any identified record shall file a request addressed to the System Manager indicating whether the individual intends to appear in person or desires to receive a copy by mail.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requests must specify preferred method of access (in-person inspection or mailed copy).

rubrics_metrics.name: Identification for in-person access (§455.4(a))
rubrics_metrics.description: An individual appearing in person shall do so at the Commission's offices during business hours and present a form of identification (e.g., valid driver’s license or employee ID) permitting verification that the individual is the one named in the record requested.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies place, hours (1325 G Street NW, 8:30 A.M.–5:00 P.M., Mon–Fri), and acceptable ID examples to verify identity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identification for mailed copies (§455.4(b))
rubrics_metrics.description: An individual desiring mail delivery shall include in the request the date and location of birth of the individual as suitable proof of identity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When requesting mailed copies, supply birth date and birth location as identity proof.

rubrics_metrics.name: Alternative identity verification (§455.4(c))
rubrics_metrics.description: Where standard forms of identification are not feasible or appropriate, the Commission shall request a signed statement asserting identity and acknowledging criminal penalties for obtaining records under false pretenses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Signed statement must assert identity and show awareness of penalty (fine up to $5,000) for false pretenses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disclosure upon verification (§455.5)
rubrics_metrics.description: Upon verification of identity, the System Manager shall disclose: (a) the information contained in the record pertaining to that individual; and (b) the accounting of disclosures of the record, if any, required by 5 U.S.C. 552a(c).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Disclosure includes both record contents and statutorily required disclosure accounting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Request for correction/amendment content (§455.6)
rubrics_metrics.description: An individual may request that a record be amended or corrected by submitting a request in accordance with §455.3 and stating the item to be amended and specific reasons therefor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Correction requests must identify the specific item and provide reasons for the change.

rubrics_metrics.name: Agency review timeline for correction requests (§455.7)
rubrics_metrics.description: Within ten days of receipt of a correction request, the System Manager will acknowledge receipt and either (a) make the correction/amendment and inform the individual, or (b) inform the individual of refusal, the reason, and procedures to request a review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 10‑day acknowledgment and prompt action or notice of refusal with review procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appeal of adverse correction determination (§455.8)
rubrics_metrics.description: An individual may request review of the System Manager's refusal by the Chairman; the Chairman will complete review within 30 days (extendable for good cause). If Chairman also refuses, the individual may file a concise statement of disagreement and seek judicial review under 5 U.S.C. 552a(g)(1)(A).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Chairman review timeframe (30 days), extension for good cause, and right to submit statement and seek judicial review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accompaniment for in-person disclosure (§455.9)
rubrics_metrics.description: An individual to whom a record is disclosed in person may have a person of his or her choosing accompany the individual when the record is disclosed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Allows a companion to be present during in-person record disclosure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Privacy Act fees for search, review, and necessary copying (§455.10(a))
rubrics_metrics.description: The Commission will not charge an individual for the costs of making a search for a record or the costs of reviewing the record; necessary copies made as part of disclosure will not be charged.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Search and review are free; copies made as necessary for disclosure are free.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fees for requested copies (Privacy Act) (§455.10(b))
rubrics_metrics.description: If an individual requests a copy of the record when a copy has not otherwise been made as necessary to disclose, the Commission will charge $0.25 per page to the extent the request exceeds $5.00 in cost to the Commission; requests not exceeding $5.00 will be met without cost.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Per‑page charge $0.25 applies only when the total cost to the Commission exceeds $5.00.

rubrics_metrics.name: Criminal penalties for false statements and false pretenses (§455.11)
rubrics_metrics.description: 18 U.S.C. 1001 makes it a crime (max fine $10,000 or 5 years imprisonment) to knowingly and willfully make false statements; 5 U.S.C. 552a(i)(3) makes it a misdemeanor (max $5,000) to knowingly and willfully request or obtain any record under false pretenses; 552a(i)(1) and (2) provide penalties for agency employee violations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explains potential criminal/misdemeanor penalties for misuse or false statements in the request process.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exemption availability (Privacy Act) (§455.12)
rubrics_metrics.description: No Commission records system is exempted from the provisions of 5 U.S.C. 552a except as permitted under certain conditions by 5 U.S.C. 552a(j) and (k).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Indicates that only statutory (j)/(k) exemptions may apply to Commission systems.

rubrics_metrics.name: General FOIA policy to facilitate availability (§456.4(a))
rubrics_metrics.description: The Commission's general policy is to facilitate the broadest possible availability and dissemination of information to the public; staff will assist the public formally or informally and may disclose records in the public interest to the extent permitted by other laws.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Staff assistance is available; informal disclosure permitted if consistent with regulations and other laws; public interest disclosure may be made when authorized.

rubrics_metrics.name: Official place and hours for obtaining information (§456.4(b))
rubrics_metrics.description: Information may be obtained only from the Commission's offices at 1325 G Street, NW, Washington, DC, official hours 8:00 a.m. to 6:00 p.m., Monday through Friday, excluding legal holidays.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies physical location and official hours for public access.

rubrics_metrics.name: Correct information source routing and effect on time limit (§456.4(c))
rubrics_metrics.description: Requests for publications or general info should go to Public Affairs; formal FOIA requests must go to the Freedom of Information Officer. Wrongly directed requests will be routed and the ten‑day Commission determination period does not begin until the request reaches or should have reached the appropriate source.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Routing errors delay the statutory 10‑day determination start; internal routing by staff is required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Types of information routinely available (§456.4(d))
rubrics_metrics.description: The following shall be routinely available (subject to fees) without a formal FOIA request unless exempt: (1) correspondence between Commission and the public; (2) Executive Director’s Recommendations; (3) Committee Reports; (4) Commission Memorandums of Actions; and (5) Maps.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Map requests directed to Public Affairs; other listed items to Freedom of Information Officer.

rubrics_metrics.name: Formal FOIA request content and labeling (§456.4(e))
rubrics_metrics.description: All formal FOIA requests must be in writing to the Freedom of Information Officer, with 'Freedom of Information Request' on the envelope, state that the request is made pursuant to FOIA, reasonably describe the information sought (including dates if known), state the maximum fee the requester is willing to pay, and provide a telephone number if possible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides content and procedural labeling to expedite handling and fee handling.

rubrics_metrics.name: FOIA 10‑day determination and notice of right to appeal (§456.4(f))
rubrics_metrics.description: The Freedom of Information Officer shall determine within ten days (except Saturdays, Sundays, legal holidays) whether to comply and immediately notify the requester of the determination, reasons, and right to appeal any adverse determination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Timely written notice required; suspension and extension rules apply under 'unusual circumstances.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition and examples of 'unusual circumstances' for FOIA extensions (§456.4(f))
rubrics_metrics.description: Unusual circumstances (permitting extension up to ten working days by written notice) include: (1) need to search for and collect records from establishments separate from the Commission's offices; (2) need to search/collect/examine a voluminous amount of separate and distinct records demanded in a single request; (3) need for consultation, with all practicable speed, with another agency with substantial interest or among components with substantial subject matter interest.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Extension notice must set forth reasons and expected decision date; cannot extend more than ten working days.

rubrics_metrics.name: Content of notice when granting a FOIA request (§456.4(g))
rubrics_metrics.description: If granting in whole or part, the notice shall describe the information to be made available, state the time and place for inspection or procedures for duplication/delivery, and state total fees chargeable according to fee schedule.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Notice must provide logistical and fee details for access/delivery.

rubrics_metrics.name: Denial notice and appeal procedure for FOIA (§456.4(h))
rubrics_metrics.description: If denying in whole or part, the FOI Officer shall notify in writing; any appeal must be in writing to the Chairman, include a brief statement of the legal/factual basis for objection; the Chairman shall determine within 20 days (except weekends/holidays) and notify the party with reasons.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies appeal channel (Chairman), content of appeal, and 20‑day decision timeline.

rubrics_metrics.name: FOIA procedural waiver authority (§456.4(i))
rubrics_metrics.description: The Freedom of Information Officer may waive any procedural requirement when a waiver would further the Act by causing public disclosure of nonconfidential information within the statutory time period.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Allows discretionary expedited handling to further FOIA purposes.

rubrics_metrics.name: FOIA fee schedule (categories and per-item rates) (§456.4(j)(1))
rubrics_metrics.description: Commission may charge: publications as marked; Commission reports $0.25/page; Committee reports $0.25/page; Commission Memorandums of Actions $0.25/page; transcripts $0.25/page; other records $0.25/page; map publications: microfilm printout $1.00 each; ozalid maps $0.30/linear foot; manual record research $2.25/quarter hour (clerical) or $5.00/quarter hour (professional); review charges $5.00/quarter hour. The Commission may charge search/review costs even if no disclosure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Detailed per-item fee schedule and rates for manual research and review; charges may apply even when records are ultimately withheld.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requester classification and fee treatment (§456.4(j)(2))
rubrics_metrics.description: Fee rules depend on requester class: (i) commercial use: may be charged all direct costs of search/review/duplication and Commission will evaluate the use; (ii) educational and non‑commercial scientific institutions: charged reproduction cost alone excluding first 100 pages; must show institutional qualification and non‑commercial use; (iii) news media: reproduction cost alone excluding first 100 pages; (iv) all other requesters: may be charged fees to recover full reasonable direct costs excluding first 100 pages and first two hours of search time. Requests by record subjects are treated under Privacy Act fee provisions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Classification affects which costs can be recovered; Commission may infer use if not explained by requester.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limited complimentary back copies policy (§456.4(j)(3))
rubrics_metrics.description: The Commission keeps a limited quantity of back copies of certain documents (Executive Director’s Recommendations, Committee Reports, Memorandums). It will attempt to fill requests from back copies at no charge until supply is exhausted; thereafter the fee schedule applies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Free copies while limited supply exists; afterward normal fees apply.

rubrics_metrics.name: No‑charge threshold and minimum fee; public interest fee waiver (§456.4(j)(4)–(5))
rubrics_metrics.description: The Commission may not charge if cost of collecting fee would equal or exceed the fee. Minimum fee is $2.00 (over free first 100 pages and 2 hours of search time). The FOI Officer may waive or reduce fees if disclosure is in the public interest (likely to contribute significantly to public understanding of government operations and not primarily in the requester’s commercial interest). Factors considered include subject of request, informative value, contribution to public understanding, significance of the contribution, existence/magnitude of commercial interest, and whether disclosure is primarily in the commercial interest of the requester.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sets threshold/minimum and enumerates factors to evaluate fee waivers for public interest.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prior fee approval and advance deposit rules (§456.4(k))
rubrics_metrics.description: If estimated charges likely to exceed $25, the agency shall notify the requester of estimated amount unless requester pre‑agreed. If fees are likely to exceed $250, the Commission may require advance payment in whole or part. Prior unpaid fees may trigger requirement to pay prior balance and advance payment for new requests. Request for fee approval/advance deposit suspends FOIA response period. The Commission may aggregate multiple requests reasonably believed to be attempts to evade fees.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Estimates trigger notification; >$250 may trigger advance deposit; suspension effect on statutory clock; anti‑evasion aggregation policy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Payment methods for FOIA fees (§456.4(l))
rubrics_metrics.description: Fees must be paid in full prior to release; payment by personal check, postal money order, or bank draft on a U.S. bank payable to the Treasurer of the United States.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies acceptable payment instruments and prepayment requirement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition: direct costs, search, duplication, review (§456.3)
rubrics_metrics.description: Direct costs are expenditures actually incurred in searching, duplicating and reviewing records; search includes all time spent looking for material responsive to a request; duplication refers to making a copy; review refers to examining located documents for commercial use requests to determine permitted withholdings and processing documents for disclosure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These definitions control what may be charged and how time/costs are calculated.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition: commercial use requester (§456.3(e))
rubrics_metrics.description: A commercial use request is from or on behalf of one who seeks information to further commercial, trade or profit interests of the requester or on whose behalf the request is made.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Determines fee treatment and whether full direct costs may be charged.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition: educational and non‑commercial scientific institutions (§456.3(f),(g))
rubrics_metrics.description: Educational institution: preschool, elementary/secondary, institutions of undergraduate/graduate/professional/vocational education operating scholarly research programs. Non‑commercial scientific institution: non‑profit operated solely for scientific research whose results are not intended to promote a product or industry.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These categories receive reduced fee treatment (reproduction cost alone excluding first 100 pages) if use qualifies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition: representative of the news media (§456.3(h))
rubrics_metrics.description: Person actively gathering news for an entity organized to publish or broadcast news to the public; 'news' means information about current events or of current public interest. Freelance journalists may qualify if they demonstrate a solid basis for expecting publication.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: News media classification excludes commercial use and entitles requesters to reproduction cost treatment (first 100 pages free).

rubrics_metrics.name: Self-evaluation requirement under section 504 (§457.110(a))
rubrics_metrics.description: The agency shall, by August 24, 1987, evaluate its current policies and practices and their effects that do not or may not meet the requirements of this part, and proceed to make necessary modifications to the extent required.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mandates a self-audit of policies/practices for compliance with nondiscrimination on the basis of handicap.

rubrics_metrics.name: Opportunity for public participation in self-evaluation (§457.110(b))
rubrics_metrics.description: The agency shall provide interested persons, including handicapped persons or organizations representing handicapped persons, an opportunity to participate in the self-evaluation process by submitting comments (oral and written).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requires outreach and inclusion of affected stakeholders in the evaluation process.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition: auxiliary aids (section 504)
rubrics_metrics.description: Auxiliary aids means services or devices enabling persons with impaired sensory, manual, or speaking skills to participate equally, e.g., readers, brailled materials, audio recordings, TDDs, note takers, interpreters, written materials.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Lists examples to guide accommodation decisions under section 504.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition: complete complaint (section 504)
rubrics_metrics.description: A complete complaint is a written statement with complainant’s name and address, describing the alleged discriminatory action in sufficient detail to inform the agency of nature and date of alleged violation, signed by complainant or authorized representative; class/third‑party complaints must identify alleged victims by name if possible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sets minimum content for administrative complaints of discrimination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition: handicapped person and related subcriteria (section 504)
rubrics_metrics.description: Handicapped person means any person with a physical or mental impairment substantially limiting one or more major life activities, has a record of such impairment, or is regarded as having such impairment. Includes list of physiological and mental conditions and explanation of 'major life activities,' 'has a record of,' and 'is regarded as.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Substantive definition for determining who is protected by section 504; gives illustrative conditions and tests for coverage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition: qualified handicapped person (section 504)
rubrics_metrics.description: Qualified handicapped person defined in contexts: (1) education services: member of class otherwise entitled to receive services; (2) programs requiring performance: meets essential eligibility requirements and can achieve purpose without modifications that would fundamentally alter program; (3) other programs: meets essential eligibility requirements to participate or receive benefits; (4) employment: defined by 29 CFR 1613.702(f).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Establishes the tests for qualification across program contexts; links employment standard to other federal regulation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition: substantial impairment (historic preservation context)
rubrics_metrics.description: Substantial impairment means a significant loss of the integrity of finished materials, design quality, or special character resulting from a permanent alteration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used to assess physical impacts to historic properties under program accessibility standards.
